entries.8c73451de9bfc341: A business that manufactures and sells architectural products such as door closers (devices that close doors quietly), hinges and architectural hardware. This business is carried out by the company and Liyoubi Construction Technology (Dalian) Co., Ltd. in China. In August 2024, the company became a subsidiary; it had taken over the architectural products business through a company split of Kyocera Liyoubi (Dalian) Machinery Co., Ltd., which had been an equity-method affiliate. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥10,874 million, down 1.5% from the previous year. The company explains that revenue declined in both Japan and overseas.
entries.8fe3fe8505f48079: A business that produces die-cast products and aluminum castings, which become parts for automobiles and other vehicles, accounting for the majority of the group's revenue. Die-casting is a method of pouring molten metal such as aluminum into a mold to form parts. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥274,310 million, up 6.4% from the previous year. The company explains that revenue increased in both Japan and overseas, due to higher production volume by weight from the recovery in automobile production and the effect of aluminum raw material prices. Operations are carried out by domestic subsidiaries including Ryobi Mirasaka Co., Ltd., Ryobi Mitsugi Co., Ltd., Tokyo Keigokin Seisakusho Co., Ltd., Ikuno Co., Ltd. (aluminum secondary alloy ingots), Hoei Kogyo Co., Ltd. (aluminum forgings) and Fuji Kogyo Co., Ltd. (die-cast product processing), and by manufacturing companies in the United States, Mexico, the United Kingdom, China and Thailand, with 17 companies in total including the company. The main customers are Ford Motor (revenue of ¥38,790 million for the fiscal year ended December 2025, 12.5% of total sales) and General Motors (¥34,032 million, 11.0%), both of which are customers of this business.
